name: Directory Of Unsheltered Street Homeless To General Population Ratio 2011
description:
This dataset compares the size of the unsheltered street homeless population to the general population for eight major U.S. cities in 2011. Each row represents one city and includes the city name, the count of people living unsheltered on the street, the city's total general population, and the resulting ratio of unsheltered homeless residents to the overall population (expressed as "1 in N"). The cities covered include Washington, DC, Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York City, and Chicago, among others.

The data can be used to compare the relative scale of street homelessness across large cities, to identify places with unusually high or low rates of unsheltered homelessness, and to support reporting, policy analysis, or advocacy around housing and social services. Because the ratio is already calculated, users can quickly rank or contrast cities without additional computation, while the raw population counts allow for further analysis or charting.
